title: UserPack
description: A user-authored / imported DATA MODULE (F-42 / UD-1, ruling user-data-editor-foundations-concept G4). One pack is a namespaced set of FULL RECORD overrides + additions across any content section. The always-present local pack ('My Data') plus any number of imported packs live in IndexedDB (swrpg_user_packs); a registry loader applies the active packs at its single funnel via SWRPGMods.applyOverlay (base -> community -> user, last-write-wins in that documented order). Local user data + module import are FREE app functionality; only HOSTING/sync is ever a paid rung (F-34 line).
$comment: G4 CONTRACT (SETTLED 2026-07-17, delegated research + Jason). FULL-RECORD overlays, not field-deltas — every mature analog's default, and it sidesteps the JSON-Patch array traps our nested records (talent trees, qualities) would hit. Overriding a canonical id (verbatim, that id) is the deliberate act; a NEW record is namespaced custom_<pack>_<slug> so collision with a canonical id is structurally impossible. NO deletes in v1 (redefine or add; hiding is what shelf toggles do). Each override carries _base {version-or-hash, editedAt} so the app detects errata drift at load. Repeated edits overwrite in place: ONE current copy per record per pack, zero version growth. A section record is validated against ITS canonical schema (weapon.schema, species.schema, ...) at pack-load — this schema governs only the PACK ENVELOPE.

formatVersion.description: Pack envelope version. Bumps only on a breaking envelope change; readers branch on it (R-Y2-1 class).

packId.description: Stable pack identity; the namespace segment in custom_<packId>_<slug> and the key in swrpg_user_packs. The always-present local pack is 'my_data'. No hyphen (ruling f100-ud1-contracts R-FUD-2): entity ids are ^[a-z0-9_]+$, so a hyphenated packId would mint custom_ ids that fail their own entity schema; no ':' or '@' either, so the user:<packId>@<v12> stamp parses unambiguously.

instance.description: OWN packs only (ruling f100-editor-contracts-2 R-EC2-1): this collection's identity, minted ONCE at creation from the platform's cryptographic RNG (48 bits, 12 lowercase hex), never derived from content, name or clock, so two fresh empty 'My Data' collections never share one. An own pack's character stamp is user:<packId>#<instance>. Carried by the FULL export; a SHARE never carries it (H8(a)). On an imported pack it is inert (imported stamps are user:<packId>@<v12>).

name.description: Human-facing pack name shown in the pack manager.

_provenance.description: Marks every record reached through this pack as user/homebrew — never masquerades as canon (standing transparency law; the honesty that keeps free-edit safe).

attribution.description: Optional author/source credit for an imported/shared pack (mirrors the mod manifest's attribution).

createdAt.description: ISO timestamp (pass-in; stamped by the editor, never derived at load).

updatedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the last edit to any record in the pack.

projection.description: OPTIONAL (ruling f100-ud1-contracts R-FUD-8, brief §8). full (the default, and what an absent value means) = every record is a FULL record (G4): the local store and the FULL backup export. share = the EXPORT FOR SHARING projection: a plain add is emitted whole; a derive is emitted as { _mode: 'derive', _base: <anchor of the LIVE base, with its id>, _changes: P }, P computed as a redefine's (f100-editor-contracts-2 R-EC2-2); a redefine or derive whose book record this app lacks, or a redefine of another pack's book-rooted record, is LEFT OUT (R-EC2-3); a redefine of a canonical id is emitted as { _mode: 'redefine', _base: <anchor of the LIVE base at export>, _changes: <RFC 7386 merge patch over the p1 projections> }, never carrying an unchanged base leaf. A receiver stores the file as received and rebuilds each share record at load as MergePatch(p1(its live base), _changes) (R-FUD-10).

sections.description: id -> FULL RECORD per section. Override when the id exists in base; addition (custom_ id) when it doesn't. An absent section is simply not overlaid. Every section the app's registries expose is available; a pack carries only the sections it touches.

$patch.description: OPTIONAL (ruling f100-items-share-residual R-FISR-1/2): the RFC 7386 merge patch that turns the book's element $base into the user's (diffShare's rules: p1 decides, raw emits, nested arrays of objects by element). $base is the book element giving the SMALLEST patch; the receiver merges this over its own book's element $base.

baseElementRef.description: An ELEMENT REFERENCE inside a share's `_changes` array (ruling f100-items-editor-contracts R-FIEC-2; f100-items-share-residual R-FISR-1): 'the book record's element at this index' — unchanged, or with `$patch` merged over it. It stands for a book sentence the share must not carry (R-SC-1). Never stored in a FULL record; formatVersion stays 1 (nothing had shipped).

recordMap.description: id -> FULL record (G4). Each value is validated against its section's entity schema at the pack boundary AFTER the pack-owned keys (_base, _mode, _changes) are set aside. The key equals the record's `id`.

_mode.description: add = a NEW record started blank; its id MUST be custom_<packId>_<slug> when authored, and an add whose id is canonical is refused (D-PS3). derive = a NEW record the user started FROM a book record (ruling f100-editor-drc-census-share-copy R-SC-2; f100-editor-contracts-2 R-EC2-2): the id rules of an add, plus a _base naming the book record's id. redefine = the deliberate override of an existing id, by that id verbatim (a canonical id, or another pack's id). Written on EVERY record the app authors or imports; a reader tolerates its absence by deriving it (canonical id -> redefine, else add; never derive).

_from.description: OWN LAYER ONLY (ruling f100-m13-layer R-M13L-16): the layer a character's modified copy was taken from: 'base', a variant stamp or a user: stamp. Any other pack carrying it reads as an unknown field.

_changes.description: SHARE projection only (projection: share): the RFC 7386 merge patch over the book record's p1 that rebuilds this record (R-FUD-8/10). A changed array of OBJECTS ships element by element (ruling f100-items-editor-contracts R-FIEC-2): an element p1-equal to a book element ships as #/$defs/baseElementRef, any other element whole; an array of plain values ships whole. The receiver swaps each reference for its own book's element at that index before the merge; a reference to an element its book lacks keeps the record, not applied. Validated by the rebuild, not here (a record's `_changes` is set aside with the other pack-owned keys).

baseAnchor.description: The CANONICAL base record's fingerprint at edit time (R-FPA-2). Written by the app on every redefine of a canonical id (the base is the record's own key; no id) and on every derive (the base is named by id, R-SC-2 / R-EC2-2); absent on a plain add and on a redefine of another pack's id, except that a character's own-layer redefine carries it whichever layer it copied (f100-m13-layer R-M13L-16). The app compares ref against the live base's fingerprint at load to decide the record's base state; the tag never decides anything.

id.description: derive only: the id of the canonical record this one was started from, in the SAME section. The receiving app shows that record's name, resolved at render against its own book data (R-SC-4); the file carries no name.

ref.description: <algorithm>:<projection>:<hex>. v1 writes sha256:p1:<64 hex> = SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 JCS serialisation of the base record's p1 projection (top-level _* keys excluded, null members dropped at every depth, arrays in order). The pattern is deliberately wider than what v1 writes: a ref written by a newer app must LOAD (as unverifiable), not fail validation.

tag.description: OPTIONAL retrieval hint: the app build the base was read from (__HOLOCRON_BUILD__, the CF_PAGES_COMMIT_SHA that /version.json's `build` also carries; 'dev-<ms>' locally). For readable text ('made against build 1f0f1bbc') and a future three-way diff when historical registries are retrievable. Never compared for drift.

fields.description: OPTIONAL (ruling f100-items-editor-contracts R-FIEC-3 (a)): per OWNED field of the book record at anchor time (every non-_ key except sources, null ≡ absent), the first 12 hex of SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 JCS of the field's p1 value. Hashes only, no book text. Taken with the anchor, re-taken on reconcile, restored with the prior anchor on Undo. The split: the book changed a field when its current hash differs (a key it added or removed included); you changed it when your value's does; both is a conflict. Every user-facing 'the book changed' signal reads the split; an anchor without it falls back to `ref`.

editedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the edit that captured this anchor (unchanged from the UD-0 text).
